newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African gilts closed sporting lower yields Thursday after a prolonged battle against technical resistance.
The benchmark R150 long bond was last at 14.04 percent from Wednesday's close of 14.115 percent.

The bellwether bounced off a 17-month low of 14.02 percent several times shortly after the open but succumbed to afternoon profit takers up to 14.08 percent after it became clear the big figure would not be breached.
Dealers said the 14.00 percent level would grow more resilient as August bond options closeout neared.
South African bond options expire in 14 days time.

"We have a come a fair way and the R150's supported near the option closeout. We think that we're going to see it try the 14.03 area once more before going back to 14.20," opined one Johannesburg-based bond dealer.
Some dealers continued to punt on the 14.00 percent break occuring in the traditionally volatile unofficial dealings after the close but did not expect such a move to hold into Friday's session.
The rand closed stronger but rangebound with U.K. banks selling dollars over the afternoon but the broader market apparently reluctant to pare dollar positions too much given offshore strength.
Cross rate action saw the local unit back above 40 pfennigs as it tracked U.S. dollar gains. The rand was last changing hands at 0.4025/4029 from 0.3999/4005 Wednesday.
Against the yen, the rand was fetching 25.4462/4849 from a previous level of 25.3641/3918. It clawed its way back into the black against the British pound at 7.6255/6351 from 7.6728/6824.
On the money market, offered rates for three-month NCDs fell to between 15.60 to 15.65 percent, while the 90-day BA rate dropped to between 15.00 and 15.10 percent.
The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage fell to 7.860 billion rand on Wednesday from 8.777 billion rand on Tuesday.
While the shortage has narrowed for the second day running it remains well above the 5.901 billion at which it began the month.
Wednesday's Bond Exchange turnover rose to 11 billion rand from 8.86 billion rand on Tuesday.
